transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Jordan Lee (Redwood); David Ortiz, Priya Singh, Marcus Allen (Emerald Bank)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Weekly POC security sync focusing on SSO/SAML test plan, audit log retention, SOC2 artifacts mapping, and discussion of hosted vs private deployment constraints. Agreed next steps to exchange artifacts and run SSO test in staging.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intro, I'm Maya, account owner for Emerald Bank, Jordan is our solutions engineer. How are we doing?
[00:08] David Ortiz: Good, thanks. We wanted to focus mostly on the security checklist items today, SSO and audit logs, and then timing for SOC2 review.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Yep, that's the plan. Jordan, you want to kick off with SSO notes?
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Sure. So we validated the metadata you sent last week — thanks Priya — and Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and OIDC, depending on your IdP. For the POC we recommend SAML in staging so we can test with assertion flows. A couple of caveats — if you plan to use our hosted API, tokens are short-lived and we keep an audit trail, if you go Private/VPC we can give you a private control plane and you control key management.
[00:45] Priya Singh: Quick question, when you say "audit trail", what fields are captured? We need user, action, timestamp, model id, request_id, also the redaction level for PII.
[00:55] Jordan Lee: Good Q. Our logs include request_id, timestamp, route, model variant, token usage counts, and username if upstream SSO mapping is provided. We also capture any error codes. PII is not stored by default in payloads, but if you enable debug logs you can get more detail — we recommend encrypting debug exports and only enabling them for short windows.
[01:20] Marcus Allen: Are the logs pushable to our SIEM? Splunk or S3?
[01:25] Jordan Lee: Yes — we support push to S3 buckets and can forward to Splunk/Datadog via syslog or an event bridge. For hosted customers we have a logs export pipeline; for Dedicated/Private you can host the exporter in your network.
[01:40] David Ortiz: What's the retention window? We need to match bank policy — 7 years is our extreme, but for this pilot we need 1 year minimum for transaction meta.
[01:50] Maya Chen: We should clarify: retention for production differs, for POC we typically recommend 90 days but we can configure per-customer if you're on Dedicated or Private.
[02:05] Priya Singh: So for hosted, is retention configurable on the tenant side? Or does Redwood set default?
[02:12] Jordan Lee: Hosted has a default retention (30 days for payload-lite logs, 90 for metadata). We can make exceptions under enterprise contracts or recommend Dedicated so you control retention. Also note export hooks let you stream to your S3 for long-term archiving.
[02:30] David Ortiz: Ok, good. On KMS — does Redwood manage keys for hosted? Or do we bring our own?
[02:36] Jordan Lee: For hosted we manage encryption at rest keys. We support AWS KMS integration for Dedicated/Private deployments where you can supply CMKs. We also support HSM integrations for high-compliance customers.
[02:50] Priya Singh: Are logs encrypted client-side or server-side?
[02:53] Jordan Lee: Server-side by default. If you want client-side encryption you can implement envelope encryption before hitting the API, but that's more effort. We can share guidance.
[03:05] [Crosstalk] Marcus Allen: got it, thanks.
[03:10] Maya Chen: David, you mentioned SOC2 mapping. Jordan has a SOC2 packet we can share.
[03:14] David Ortiz: Yes, we'll need to see control mappings and the latest report if possible. That's key for us to move beyond POC.
[03:22] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — we'll send the SOC2 Type II summary and a controls mapping doc. Note some of the infra controls depend on whether you're on-hosted or private, so we'll annotate those.
[03:35] Priya Singh: Can you also indicate which controls remain customer responsibility? For example identity management and network segmentation.
[03:41] Jordan Lee: Yep, that's in the mapping doc. We'll flag SSO, MFA enforcement, network ACLs, and KMS as customer responsibilities when using Private.
[03:50] [07:05] Maya Chen: Switching to SSO test plan — Priya, do you have a test IdP account ready?
[07:12] Priya Singh: I can create a test account tomorrow. Do you need metadata or do you prefer the IdP metadata XML?
[07:18] Jordan Lee: IdP metadata XML is easiest. We'll take your metadata and add Redwood service provider details — ACS URL, entity ID. For staging we can use a generic redirect URI. We'll do one end-to-end login and then verify the SAML attributes map to username/email.
[07:35] Priya Singh: For attribute mapping, can we map Azure AD groups to RBAC roles? We need role-based access for console vs API keys.
[07:45] Jordan Lee: Yes, group-to-role mapping is supported. On hosted we map SAML groups to Redwood roles; on Private you can sync via SCIM or local LDAP. We'll send sample SAML attribute mapping.
[07:58] Marcus Allen: Any gotchas around session length and token expiry? Our security policy wants short sessions and immediate revocation on logout.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: Sessions are configurable. Token TTL is short by default (15 minutes for access tokens); refresh tokens depend on deployment. For immediate revocation we support session invalidation via an admin API — but for hosted environments the propagation can be a few seconds. For Private you can make it immediate.
[08:25] David Ortiz: Regarding privacy: do you retain request payloads, and if so can we enable automatic redaction of PII?
[08:32] Jordan Lee: By default request payloads are not stored in full. We store metadata and token counts. We offer a redaction layer that removes common PII patterns; it's not perfect and we recommend pre-redaction client-side for highly sensitive data.
[08:50] Priya Singh: For our POC, we will not send full account numbers, but we will want to see sample outputs and latency numbers. Are there any security considerations for running benchmarks?
[08:59] Jordan Lee: Benchmarks are fine; we'll provide safe test sequences. If you need internal-only data, run it in a Private environment. Latency metrics are captured in the console per-request with token-level breakdowns.
[09:15] Maya Chen: Quick note on audit log export: Jordan, could you provide a sample log line so David's team can confirm fields?
[09:21] Jordan Lee: Sure, I'll attach a sample in the follow-up email. It includes timestamp, request_id, model, route, user_id (if SSO mapped), tokens_in/tokens_out, status_code.
[09:35] David Ortiz: Great. Also, regulatory asks: does Redwood have any regional data residency guarantees? We need EU only for EU customers.
[09:42] Jordan Lee: Yes — region pinning is available on Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have region options but not hard residency guarantees unless we agree in contract. We'll note that in the SOC2 mapping.
[09:58] Priya Singh: One operational question: for debugging annotated responses, how do we request them without exposing PII?
[10:05] Jordan Lee: Use a debug flag that writes to a temporary debug bucket with TTL and encryption; we advise using synthetic data in debug windows.
[10:15] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps before finishing. Maya to send pricing and security packet — Jordan to send SOC2 mapping and sample logs — Priya to provide IdP metadata and test account — schedule SSO run on 3/16. Anything else?
[10:30] Marcus Allen: We'll also confirm retention target for logs and whether we want hosted or Dedicated for pilot.
[10:35] David Ortiz: I'll review the SOC2 docs once you share and get back with legal/reg compliance comments by next Tuesday.
[10:42] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll follow up with a single email thread with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the SSO session. Thanks everyone.
[10:50] Priya Singh: Thanks all.
[11:00] [End of recording]
